reviews.comment: If you want to actually learn content in lecture, then don't bother taking him. If you're familiar with Fords exams, then the class isn't difficult as he administers the same exams Ford gives for his sections. The final exam is however, made by Finkelstein, but all questions are slightly altered versions of fords exam questions.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If this guy is the only prof with seats open, sign up. Just plan on attending another professor's lectures.

His lectures consist of him confusing himself, going over ONLY theoretical things, no practice probs, and you can barely understand him. If you get stuck with him, drop it. Your only hope it reading the textbook, or going to another profs lecture. If get him, I hope you have a god to pray to, because that is the only way you can pass this class.

Lectures consist of him reading off the textbook pages in a thick accent. Grades are not accessible on canvas. You must manually calculate grades from lab, homework, and exams. Exam grades are only accessible if you collect the exam at the end of the first lecture after the exam, so if you miss that lecture, you cannot learn how you did.

This was the most important class I took, not because the professor was great, but because he wasn't. It showed me that learning is entirely on me. I am grateful to Dr. Finkelstein for teaching me this invaluable lesson indirectly. I highly recommend you take this course.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Appallingly horrible professor. Cannot communicate with students, and doesn't even seem to have an understanding of the material. Cannot use technology, and often called for campus tech support during lectures to help connect to HDMI. The day of an exam, he tried solving a potential exam question for the class, couldn't get the answer, and gave up.

Dr. Finkelstein is the opposite of what you want for PHYS 202. He doesn't communicate well, has a thick accent, not engaging at all, isn't tech savvy, etc. He's just a bad prof overall. I only did well because of Organic Chemistry Tutor and doing 5-6 practice exams per test. It's doable to get a good grade, but don't take him at all!

AVOID. couldn't understand him because of his accent. he needs to retire bc he doesn't know how to work technology. would show up to exams late which was extremely unprofessional and rude. you can get by if you teach yourself using the previous year's exams but if you need an A , I'd recommend taking someone who will actually teach you.

I personally got nothing from the lectures and managed by teaching myself and doing a lot of practice tests. He is agreeable, but I could not learn anything in the class. This class is very doable if you either pay attention or study on your own. This semester there were a lot of left field questions on the exams (Ford), which was frustrating.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Avoid Finkelstein if you can. The lectures are useless and almost no one goes except to pick up his exams. Idek how he doesn't realize hes a bad prof with like 5 people regularly attending lectures. His class averages are awful because students have to teach themselves physics. This course is harder than 201, if you can take it elsewhere, do it.

Finkelstein is very difficult to understand, and his lectures do nothing to prepare you for exams no matter how hard you pay attention. If you struggle with physics, take anyone but him, having him as a professor only makes physics harder than it already is. Do not take Finkelstein unless you are to ready to teach yourself the entirety of PHYS 202.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are not engaging and he teaches from slides that are basically the textbook. Most people don't bother to show up to class. I show up to class and occasionally pay attention when doing homework. He does have a thick accent, but you can get a general idea of the concepts. However, most I learned through Youtube, recitation, and old exams
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wanted to help any future students unlucky enough to take this course since the other ratings are 10 years old. Hasn't changed much from the bad ratings. VERY thick accent and hard to understand. No one goes to class because he talks the entire time about "concepts" but never gives any examples. You basically teach yourself.

I am also reviewing Mr. Finklestein to clear up the mass confusion. I am currently taking him for my physics class and it's been an honor. I do admit the tests were really hard, but he tells you what to study. The study guide as well as the lectures are more than enough. It's also vital to read the textbook, but which class doesn't. Hope this helps

Me. Finklestein changed my life. I had to take physics for my first semester during my junior year and he was amazing. Don't listen to the other 2 reviewers. If you read the book, apply you knowledge learned from the lecture, and pay attention to the minor details you will get an A. Out of my past years he was my favorite professor by far. Take him

If you read the other rating of him taking forever to make a simple, complete sentence, it's a perfect description. He speaks at a second grade reading level and loves to draw the pictures on the board that are already on the big screen he uses. HE TALKS (inaudibly) THROUGHOUT TESTS! Research is his niche, and he should stay there without teaching.

worst professor. talks to the board and has no idea what questions you are asking him. Has a thick accent and takes 1000 hours to formulate a comprehensible sentence. hardly any people showed up to the 2 hr lecture because it literally was a waste of time; you'd better off reading the book, which isn't great either.
